diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\ell$ is taken to be even in this work, $\lambda_{\ell/2+1} = -\alpha^{1/\ell}$, and {$\lambda_1 = \alpha^{1/\ell}$}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem has no hypothesis excluding the real roots. For $j=1$ or $j=\ell/2+1$, one has $\lambda_j=\Re(\lambda_j)$, so the asserted strict inequality reads $\rho(\lambda_j)<\rho(\lambda_j)$ and is false. The proof's strict inequality relies on a nonzero imaginary part.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\Im(\lambda_j)\ne0$ to the strict inequality and state equality separately for the two real roots.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false for two of the explicitly included block systems, although its intended complex-shift conclusion may remain valid.
issues.title: Strict convergence-factor inequality incorrectly includes real shifts
issues.why_classification: A short local restriction and equality case preserve the intended complex-shift bound and all rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\Re(\xi_j^{(1)})\ne\Re(\xi_j^{(N)}) $ it is straightforward to show that $\frac{| \xi_j^{(1)}-\xi_j^{(N)}| }{ |\xi_j^{(1)}| + | \xi_j^{(N)}|  } < \frac{|\xi_j^{(1)}-\xi_j^{(N)}|}{|\xi_j^{(1)}+\xi_j^{(N)}|}$ and hence for $p=1$ the Chebyshev polynomial is strictly non-optimal.

Note that, for $j' \in \{1, \ell/2 + 1\}$, 
			$\Im(\lambda_j') = 0$. Hence, $B_{j'}$ has real eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: For either real shift, both endpoint eigenvalues are positive real numbers. Consequently $|\xi_j^{(1)}|+|\xi_j^{(N)}|=|\xi_j^{(1)}+\xi_j^{(N)}|$, so the proof's strict inequality becomes equality and the degree-one Chebyshev polynomial is optimal. The proposition omits the necessary nonreal-shift hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Let $B_j$ be given by \eqref{eq:B definition}. For $p=1$ the maximal value of the optimal polynomial $\poly^*_1$ is strictly smaller than the maximum value of the scaled Chebyshev polynomial

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the proposition to $\Im(\lambda_j)\ne0$ and explicitly retain equality for the real shifts.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed strict non-optimality does not hold for all matrices $B_j$ covered by the statement.
issues.title: Non-optimality proposition is false for the real shifted systems
issues.why_classification: The intended claim about complex roots survives after a local hypothesis correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Write $H=A-\Re(\lambda_j)I$, $c=\Im(\lambda_j)$, $x_j=u+iv$, and $b_j=p+iq$. The complex equation gives $Hu+cv=p$ and $Hv-cu=q$. The displayed saddle matrix acting on $(u,-v)^T$ gives $(cu-Hv,Hu+cv)^T=(-q,p)^T$, not the displayed $(-p,q)^T$. Thus solving the stated real system generally does not recover the solution of the complex block problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed right-hand side by $(-\Im(b_j),\Re(b_j))^T$, or make an equivalent consistent permutation of equations and unknowns.
issues.overall_effect: The stated saddle-point implementation and the resulting $\mathcal P_{SP}$ application solve the wrong right-hand-side equations.
issues.title: The proposed saddle system is not equivalent to the complex block equation
issues.why_classification: A forced local correction restores exact equivalence without changing the saddle matrix, solver, cost, or preconditioning architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For complex roots $\lambda_{j}$, $j \in [2,\ell/2]\cup [\ell/2+2,\ell]$, we solve \eqref{eq:saddlesystem} using MINRES

issues.failure_explanation: In the identification supplied by the displayed saddle system, $\Phi=\Im(\lambda_j)I$. Half of the complex roots have negative imaginary part, so $\Phi$ is then negative definite, contrary to the asserted SPD hypothesis. Accordingly $\mathcal P_D=\operatorname{diag}(\Phi+\Psi,\Phi+\Psi)$ need not be positive definite, the cited SPD argument does not apply, and even in the scalar case the preconditioned eigenvalue magnitude is $\sqrt{\phi^2+\psi^2}/|\phi+\psi|>1$ when $\phi<0<\psi$, contradicting the stated interval.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of the preconditioned system $\mathcal{P}_{D}^{-1}\mathcal{S}$ lie in  $\big[-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big] \cup \big[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},1\big]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate negative-imaginary systems using $|\Im(\lambda_j)|$ with consistent sign/permutation changes, or solve only one member of each conjugate pair and reconstruct the other, then state the positivity assumptions in the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue bound and the validity of SPD-preconditioned MINRES are unsupported for all negative-imaginary roots included in the proposed $\mathcal P_{SP}$ procedure.
issues.title: Saddle-point eigenvalue theorem is applied when one block is negative definite
issues.why_classification: The overall method can plausibly be preserved, but a consistent new case treatment for half the complex shifts and its interaction with right-hand sides and conjugate reconstruction must be supplied; merely editing the theorem statement would exclude part of the advertised procedure.

We denote by  $\rho(\lambda_j)$ the

Then CI converges when applied to $B_j$, with  the error at the $p$-th iteration being bounded above by \begin{equation*}
				\frac{\| {e}_p \|_2}{\| {e}_0 \|_2} \le {\left| T_p \left(\frac{\xi_j^{(1)}+\xi_j^{(N)}}{\xi_j^{(1)}-\xi_j^{(N)}}\right) \right|}^{-1}.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence bounds only the asymptotic convergence factor, a $p$th-root limit. It does not imply the finite-iteration inequality $\|e_p\|/\|e_0\|\le\sigma_j^p$. The paper's actual per-iteration bound is the distinct Chebyshev expression in Proposition prop:errorbound, which generally includes finite-$p$ effects.

failure_location.quote: The dashed lines show an upper bound on the relative error at each iteration, which is obtained by multiplying the initial error by the upper bound on the asymptotic  convergence factor given by Theorem \ref{thm:convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the bound from Proposition prop:errorbound for the dashed curves, or relabel $\sigma_j^p$ as an asymptotic-rate proxy rather than an error upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The dashed curves and their description are not established upper bounds at every iteration, so the stated finite-iteration interpretation of the experiment is unreliable.
issues.title: An asymptotic factor is incorrectly used as a per-iteration error bound
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the plotted comparison or its interpretation leaves the asymptotic theorem and allocation heuristic intact.
